rationale: Resume the registered necessary gap (monotonic-store discriminator) whose prior run exited 1 in the harness helper's 5s shutdown timer. The harness now sets LongstopTimeout=60s and emits each scenario's CA_EVENT inside the scenario function, before the deferred cluster.Close runs, so a slow helper shutdown cannot hide a completed measurement. Scenarios, prefix, requirement and comparisons are unchanged from the predecessor.

scope.description: One process, three real Raft instances over InmemTransport with FileSnapshotStore; each scenario selects InmemStore directly (non-monotonic) or wrapped in MockMonotonicLogStore (monotonic) via MakeClusterCustom with LongstopTimeout=60s. The replacement leader compacts at or below its snapshot index (TrailingLogs=0).
assumptions: Config: ProtocolVersion=3, HeartbeatTimeout=ElectionTimeout=LeaderLeaseTimeout=300ms, CommitTimeout=10ms, TrailingLogs=0, SnapshotThreshold disabled, SnapshotInterval=1h.
The isolated node's above-snapshot suffix is produced by real uncommitted Apply calls on the old leader before it steps down; no state is injected.
MockMonotonicLogStore returns IsMonotonic()==true, so installSnapshot takes the removeOldLogs branch.
excluded: Network and TCP transports; mixed-version rolling upgrades.
Restart or recovery of the isolated node; only live catch-up is measured.

experiment.prefix: For each of three scenarios: bootstrap a 3-node cluster, commit a 20-command prefix, isolate the current leader, append 2 (control) or 200 (both stall cases) uncommitted tail commands on the isolated node, let the remaining two nodes elect a replacement leader, commit 20 more commands and take a snapshot at index S, commit 10 post entries above S, reconnect, observe for about 4.5s, and emit the scenario's setup and result events before helper cleanup. The two stall scenarios differ only in the isolated node's log store (non-monotonic vs MockMonotonicLogStore).
experiment.requirement: After a follower installs a snapshot at index S, catch-up must not depend on whether the above-S bytes survive: regardless of the LogStore's monotonicity, a follower whose persisted log ended above S must stop reporting a last log entry above S and accept the leader's AppendEntries with PrevLogEntry=S so it converges to the leader's log. Anchored in state.go:167-174 (getLastEntry) and raft.go:1475-1502 (appendEntries PrevLogEntry check); installSnapshot at raft.go:1814-1953 chooses removeOldLogs for a MonotonicLogStore and compactLogs otherwise, and is the producer responsible for the post-install last-log state.
experiment.responsibility: Follower snapshot installation establishing a post-install last-log state compatible with the leader's AppendEntries and nextIndex catch-up loop, for both monotonicity branches of the LogStore.

comparisons.description: Control: isolated log at or below the snapshot index reaches the leader commit index.
Non-monotonic store with a stale above-snapshot suffix must catch up.
Monotonic store with a stale above-snapshot suffix: removeOldLogs deletes the bytes, yet the cached last-log state must not block catch-up.

experiment.revision_reason: Harness-only change to fix the predecessor's independent cleanup failure: MakeClusterOpts.LongstopTimeout is raised from the helper default 5s to 60s, and each scenario's CA_EVENT pair is now printed inside the scenario function before the deferred cluster.Close. No scenario, app, source, requirement or comparison changed.
